what: Citable sources behind the assembl lab's twins and the Pursuit pages. Each carries a truth label the way every figure on the site does: Source (an official or peer-reviewed publication), Vendor claim (a supplier's own case study, directional only), Estimate (ours), Simulated (a twin's model output), Proposed (a change not yet made), Your data (what a customer supplies). Retrieved and checked on the date given; re-check before quoting.

sources.title: Improve patient flow, reduce length of stay and optimise providers with Digital Twin Studio
sources.useAs: The size of prize simulation can point at in an ED. A single vendor-published case: quote as a vendor claim, directional, never as a forecast for a New Zealand hospital.

sources.title: Toward a digital twin of an emergency department: agent-based architecture with Digital Shadow, Synchronised and Exploratory modes
sources.publisher: MDPI Sustainability, vol. 15, no. 4, article 3412 (University of Lorraine)

modes: Synchronised DT (mirrors and predicts between real events at an accelerated clock)
Exploratory DT (runs ensembles of possible futures for decisions)

sources.useAs: The maturity ladder the lab's maturity.json uses: model → shadow → twin (synchronised) → exploratory. Peer-reviewed; AnyLogic implementation where each real patient spawns a digital counterpart.

sources.title: 2025 Annual Grocery Report (Pūrongo ā-Tau mō te Kai)
sources.useAs: Market structure for the supermarket twin and any grocery Pursuit page. Annual: the lab serves it as the grocery snapshot feed, labelled Latest published · annual.

sources.title: Market study into supermarkets: background information (nearly $25 billion spent at supermarkets and grocery stores in the year to March 2023)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
sources.useAs: Size of the grocery market. Older than the Commission's report; say the year.

sources.title: Government Targets, Target 1: Shorter stays in emergency departments, quarterly factsheets
sources.publisher: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
sources.useAs: The national scoreboard the ED twin benchmarks against. Each factsheet reports the quarter before the one in its name. The quarterly series lives in the edhistory feed.

sources.title: Health targets: quarterly national, regional and district factsheets, and 5 and 10 years of results
sources.publisher: Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora
sources.useAs: District and national 6-hour results each quarter (the ed feed) and the ten-year same-quarter series (edhistory).

sources.title: NZ Building Outlines (LINZ Data Service layer 101290)
sources.publisher: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (attribution: Sourced from the LINZ Data Service and licensed for reuse under CC BY 4.0)
sources.useAs: The roof outline of any mainland NZ building, for a twin's 3D shell. Refreshed when a region is re-flown, not on a schedule; interiors still need plans or a scan.

sources.title: Retail trade survey, quarterly (sales and stocks by industry and region)
sources.useAs: Supermarket and hardware sales by quarter, year-on-year change and sales to stock, for the supermarket and retail twins (the rts feed).

sources.title: Did the New Zealand six-hour ED target reduce ED length of stay? A mixed-methods study
sources.publisher: BMC Health Services Research (via PubMed Central)
sources.useAs: Why the target is hard: early gains, later reliance on short-stay units, a floor near 3.5 hours' median stay. A caution against metric artefacts in any ED twin.

sources.title: Systematic review of discrete-event simulation in emergency departments (floor-plan view as step one)
sources.useAs: The nine-step ED simulation method the ED twin follows; the floor plan anchors both model logic and face validation.

sources.title: Participatory modelling with six Canadian EDs: 3D floor plans as the most effective face-validation technique
sources.useAs: Evidence that the 3D layer changes the model: clinicians corrected layouts, chair spaces and surge stretchers.
